metadata.title: Create CLI Entry Point with Typer

story.iWant: to create a basic CLI command structure using Typer
story.soThat: I can build the `bet-bot analyze` command foundation
story.tasks: - Create CLI module structure (AC: #1) - Create `/src/bet_bot/cli/` directory (if not exists) - Create `/src/bet_bot/cli/__init__.py` - Create `/src/bet_bot/cli/main.py` as entry point - Import Typer and initialize app: `app = typer.Typer()` - Implement help command and app metadata (AC: #2, #7) - Set Typer app name: `name="bet-bot"` - Set Typer app help text: `help="Positive Expected Value Detection Tool for Football Betting"` - Add version constant: `__version__ = "0.1.0"` - Implement `--version` callback that prints version and exits - Test: `python -m bet_bot.cli --help` shows help text - Test: `python -m bet_bot.cli --version` shows version - Implement analyze command stub (AC: #3, #4, #5, #6) - Create `analyze()` function decorated with `@app.command()` - Add `bankroll` parameter: `typer.Option(..., "--bankroll", "-b", help="Your betting bankroll")` - Add `config` parameter: `typer.Option(None, "--config", "-c", help="Path to config file")` - Validate bankroll is positive (raise error if <= 0) - Print confirmation message: "Starting analysis with bankroll: $X" - Add docstring explaining command purpose - Test: `python -m bet_bot.cli analyze --help` shows command help - Test: `python -m bet_bot.cli analyze --bankroll 1000` runs without error - Add input validation (AC: #4) - Validate bankroll is float type - Validate bankroll > 0 (reject negative or zero) - Show clear error message if validation fails - Test edge cases: `--bankroll 0`, `--bankroll -100`, `--bankroll abc` - Create executable entry point (AC: all) - Add `if __name__ == "__main__": app()` to main.py - Make CLI executable via `python -m bet_bot.cli` - Test: `python -m bet_bot.cli analyze --bankroll 1000` runs successfully - Documentation and validation (AC: all) - Add inline comments explaining Typer configuration - Verify all help text displays correctly - Verify error messages are user-friendly - Test all command variations work as expected

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `/src/bet_bot/cli/main.py` with Typer app setup 2. Implement basic `bet-bot --help` command 3. Implement stub `bet-bot analyze --help` command 4. Command accepts `--bankroll` argument (required, float) 5. Command accepts optional `--config` argument 6. Running `bet-bot analyze --bankroll 1000` prints "Starting analysis..." 7. Add version flag (`--version`)

doc.title: bet-bot Technical Specification
doc.snippet: CLI Framework: typer (simple, type-hinted command handling). Configuration & CLI modules handle user input, manage configurations. CLI Interface: bet-bot analyze --bankroll 1000

doc.title: bet-bot Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Purpose: Handle user input, manage configurations. Modules: main.py (Entry point, Typer CLI setup), commands.py (analyze command definition), config.py (Bankroll, API keys, preferences)

doc.title: bet-bot Project Rules - CLI Script Development
doc.snippet: ALWAYS use Typer for CLI (NOT argparse). ALWAYS use type hints for arguments. ALWAYS provide help text for all commands. ALWAYS validate inputs at CLI boundary. ALWAYS use rich for beautiful output.

python.package: CLI framework with type hints and automatic help generation
Beautiful terminal formatting (future stories will use for output)
For future input validation via Pydantic models
Backported typing features for type hints

constraints.constraint: ALWAYS use Typer for CLI (NOT argparse) - mandated by CLAUDE.md
ALWAYS use type hints for all arguments and options - mandated by Python 3.10+ requirement
ALWAYS provide help text for all commands and arguments - mandated by CLAUDE.md
ALWAYS validate inputs at CLI boundary - validation must happen before business logic
CLI layer must be thin - business logic goes in separate modules (future stories)
Use `python -m bet_bot.cli` execution pattern until proper installation - pyproject.toml entry point configured
Bankroll must be positive float - reject zero or negative values with clear error messages
Error messages must be user-friendly - never expose raw Python exceptions to users
Add version flag (--version) using Typer callback pattern - must exit immediately after printing
Keep stub implementation simple - full pipeline integration happens in Story 8.1

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest 8.4.2 with pytest-asyncio for async support. All CLI tests should be in tests/unit/test_cli.py. Use subprocess or typer.testing.CliRunner for command execution tests. Minimum 80% code coverage required. Test both success paths and error cases (invalid inputs, edge cases).
